ESA Lakes_cci · chlorophyll-a · in-situ check

Does Lakes_cci get the chlorophyll season right?

We compared Lakes_cci chlorophyll-a with 5,463 same-day field samples and with the monthly cycles of 149 lakes that have both, from North America, Europe and Mexico. In temperate lakes the seasonal timing holds up. In boreal lakes Lakes_cci peaks too early, just after ice-off, while the field data peak in July–August. The level is compressed: clear lakes read too high, very green lakes about right.

Lakes_cci v2.1 via the per-lake tables of Shahvaran et al. Why we looked

We run the GLM-AED lake model for about 40,000 lakes worldwide (ISIMIP) and validate surface chlorophyll-a against Lakes_cci. In lakes north of 40° N the model peaks in April–June, while Lakes_cci peaks in July–October. Tests with the model's growth, nutrient, grazing, nitrogen-fixation and sediment-phosphorus settings did not move the model peak. Before changing the model structure we needed to know whether the satellite timing is right. This page is that check, shared with the Lakes_cci team because the same comparison says something about the product.

North of 40° N, 80% of the field series peak in July–October. For our model this settles the question: the late-summer maximum is real, and the model's spring peak is a model problem. Lakes_cci follows the field data in temperate lakes, but north of 55° it peaks a median 1.5 months early (50% of 28 lakes two or more months early). The shift stays when only the field-sample days are used (-2 months, r -0.20), so it comes from the retrieval, not from when the satellite sees the lake: CCI reads high in May, after ice-off, in humic Finnish lakes such as Päijänne, Pielinen and Keitele. In boreal lakes Lakes_cci should not be used for timing.

Tropics. 18 lakes, nearly all Mexican reservoirs (UNEP GEMStat) plus Bosumtwi in Ghana, with a median of 26 field dates each (about three a year). CCI peaks within a month of the field data in 41% of 17 lakes, median seasonal r 0.06, and reads ×2.2 the field values. The field cycles look ten times stronger than CCI's, but with one sample per month and year most of that is sampling noise; tropical timing stays an open question. No open in-situ series exists for the large African lakes (Victoria, Tanganyika, Malawi, Kivu) or Titicaca. Brazil holds 361 tropical Lakes_cci lakes; São Paulo (CETESB) and Minas Gerais (IGAM) monitoring would add reservoirs but cannot be fetched automatically.

Australia and New Zealand. 4 lakes so far: Benmore (ECan, 103 dates): field peak Dec, CCI May, r 0.33; Ohau (ECan, 73 dates): field peak Dec, CCI May, r -0.57; Pukaki (ECan, 68 dates): field peak Mar, CCI Feb, r 0.03; Wellington (EPA Victoria, 181 dates): field peak Sep, CCI Sep, r 0.83. Lake Wellington follows the field cycle; the clear glacial lakes of Canterbury (0.5–1 µg/L) do not, as for other clear lakes. Lake Alexandrina, Taupō, Rotorua, Te Anau and Waikaremoana have monitoring that could not be fetched automatically (see Data sources).

Method

  • Lakes_cci: v2.1 merged L3S daily chlorophyll-a, summarised per HydroLAKES lake by Shahvaran et al. (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20347115, CC BY 4.0): daily lake mean, days with ≥ 10 % of the lake covered.
  • In-situ: laboratory chlorophyll-a (corrected and uncorrected for pheophytin; probe fluorescence left out), surface samples ≤ 3 m or epilimnion composites, daily mean over sites. US Water Quality Portal (waterqualitydata.us): only stations inside the HydroLAKES polygon of a Lakes_cci lake. EEA Waterbase Water Quality ICM 2026 (WISE SoE, determinand EEA_3164-01-0; values below the quantification limit set to half of it). Finnish Environment Institute VESLA open API (analyte CP, ethanol or acetone extraction). UNEP GEMStat open subset GFQA v3 (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.18459694, CC BY 4.0). Lewis et al. (2023), EDI edi.1530.1, CC BY 4.0. Local monitoring (Erken).
  • Independence: Lakes_cci chlorophyll-a algorithms were tuned and validated against LIMNADES, a research archive of bio-optical campaign data (ATBD D2.2; PVP CCI-LAKES-0030 v1.3, section 6.3, which notes that "very few data sets from national monitoring programmes" were used). LIMNADES is not used here; all values are statutory monitoring or long-term research samples, none satellite- or model-derived.
  • Pairs: same calendar day. Bias = median of log10(CCI / in-situ) per lake.
  • Seasonal cycles: monthly means per year, then the mean over years per calendar month; in-situ months need data in at least 2 years. Compared on the months both have (at least 5). Southern lakes are shifted 6 months in the pooled monthly figures.
  • Code and data: danielmerbet/lakes-cci-insitu: insitu_wqp.py, insitu_more.py, insitu_chl.py, insitu_timing.py, insitu_report.py (code GPL-3; data tables CC BY 4.0 with the source attributions).

Limits of this check

  • The tropics rest on 18 lakes sampled about three times a year; Africa has one lake, South America none.
  • Canada, Russia and China hold most Lakes_cci lakes but no open, independent series here yet. Sweden (MVM) and Canada (DataStream) need an access key; NTL-LTER needs a log-in.
  • EEA and most GEMStat records do not state the chlorophyll-a method; Finnish values are laboratory extractions.
  • Field programmes sample mostly in summer and often near shore, while CCI reports a lake mean.
  • Pheophytin-corrected and uncorrected values are pooled; the difference is usually 10–30 %.
  • This uses v2.1. The same comparison with v3.0 is being extracted now and will be added here.

Questions for the Lakes_cci team

  • In boreal humic lakes CCI peaks in May, two to four months before the field data, even on the same days. Is a post-ice-off bias known (CDOM, resuspended sediment, ice edges or the optical water type assignment)?
  • Is the higher winter–spring reading (×1.25) known, for example from low sun angles, ice edges or the optical water type mix in those months?
  • Is the compression of the range (clear lakes ×1.6–1.7 too high) expected from the OWT-blended algorithm, and does v3.0 change it?
  • Are per-pixel uncertainties for chlorophyll-a and Kd planned? They would let users weight days instead of using a fixed coverage threshold.
